name: 42347-loraprefill-8b-1gpu
model: NousResearch/Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct (bfloat16), served through the rank-256 LoRA adapter philschmid/code-llama-3-1-8b-text-to-sql-lora on every request.
hardware: 1x H100 80GB HBM3 (one GPU of an a3 node, --gres=gpu:1), sm90.
parallelism: TP=1, PP=1, DP=1, `--distributed-executor-backend uni`. One card, one in-process engine, no router.
architecture: dense LlamaForCausalLM, 32 layers, 32 query heads over 8 KV heads at head_dim 128, hidden 4096, bfloat16, ~16.1 GB of weights; the adapter is r=256, lora_alpha=128, over q/k/v/o and gate/up/down. Full config on the checkpoints.
load_profile: concurrent (closed loop), 16 streams, rate unbounded, warmup 10%, cooldown 10%, bounded at 1600 requests (1280 scored) with an 1800 s safety cap.
workload: synthetic_text, single turn, `request_format: plain`, greedy (`temperature: 0.0`), seed 1: every request is exactly 2048 prompt tokens and exactly 32 output tokens (min=max on both), prompts drawn independently, and every request is routed through the one adapter named in `scenario.json: backend.lora_modules`.
purpose: A text-to-SQL coding assistant on an 8B model with a LoRA adapter, serving 16 concurrent 2048-token prompts on one GPU.
launch:
# The engine is a source checkout at a78b842d0e85d287176031334f4721cd96b6e47d, which
# `git describe` anchors to v0.21.1rc0 -- a commit, not a release.
#
# Every request is served through one LoRA adapter. The adapter itself is named request-side, in
# `scenario.json: backend.lora_modules`, because the engine runs in-process and `--lora-modules`
# is HTTP-server surface.

model: NousResearch/Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct

enable-lora: true

# The served adapter's own rank, read off its `adapter_config.json`: the engine refuses an adapter
# whose rank exceeds this. One adapter is served, so one slot; nothing to evict.
max-lora-rank: 256
max-loras: 1

tensor-parallel-size: 1
distributed-executor-backend: uni
dtype: bfloat16

# Pinned rather than left to default: the in-process usage context does not hit the default table
# `vllm serve` resolves against, so an unpinned engine would run a different step size. At
# 2048-token prompts, 8192 is four whole prefills per step.
max-num-batched-tokens: 8192
max-num-seqs: 1024

# Prompts are drawn independently from the synthetic sampler, so there is no prefix to reuse.
enable-prefix-caching: false

# 2048 prompt + 32 output tokens; the plainest bound that clears it (the checkpoint advertises
# 131072).
max-model-len: 4096

# This engine's own default, written down so a change of default cannot move the KV pool.
gpu-memory-utilization: 0.90
